item.title: Explainable graph-based meta-reinforcement learning for cognitive UAV swarms under partial observability and adaptive jamming
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Arshad Ali, Muhammad Shaharyar Ramzan, Eraj Khan, Adeel Ahmad, Gahangir Hossain
Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning frameworks for cognitiveunmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly bundle graph coordination,meta-learning and explainability, yet it is rarely shown when that machineryactually helps. We present XM-MADRL, an explainable meta-learning graphframework for UAV swarms in contested electromagnetic environments, togetherwith a controlled study that isolates when its components pay off. Under fullobservability against a predictable jammer, coordination and meta-adaptationgive no measurable benefit: the framework merely ties a vanilla proximal policyoptimisation (PPO) baseline. Under partial observability against an adaptive,reactive jammer, the same framework is better on every spectrum metric, raisingpacket delivery ratio sixfold (16.8% versus 2.5%…

item.title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Han Zhong, Denis Kochan, Igor Žutić, Yingying Wu
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78376-1 Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits.

item.title: Hybrid quantum computer observes foundational quantum effect in a new setting
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Physicists in the Department of Physics at the University of Oxford have used a hybrid quantum computer, made up of qubits and quantum oscillators, to observe the Aharonov–Bohm effect in a quantum simulation. The effect is a quantum phenomenon in which a particle can acquire a measurable phase by traveling around a magnetic flux, even though it never passes through a region where a magnetic field is present.

item.title: Quantum chip holds multiple photons at once, opening path to scalable memory
item.description:
📚 Physics News
For highly fragile quantum information systems, the ability to store quantum information is vital—but also challenging. Quantum information is transported in particles of light called photons, which often must be temporarily paused (or "stored") while other, slower quantum operations catch up. This storage must be performed on microchips as small as 1 centimeter (0.4 inches)—a distance covered by light in a few trillionths of a second. Storing photons for a microsecond would represent a massive leap forward for the capabilities of quantum chips.

item.title: Unsteady MHD flow of Heat generating / absorbing fluid through porous plate with variable temperature and concentration in a slip flow regime
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Shaik Mubarak, M. Suryanarayana Reddy, M. C. Raju
The present study investigates the unsteady magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) free convective heat and mass transfer flow via an infinite vertical porous plate immersed in a porous material under slip flow circumstances of a viscous, incompressible, electrically conducting fluid. The plate is subjected to a consistent transverse magnetic field. The perturbation approach provides an analytical solution to the non-dimensional governing equations. Physical parameters that affect velocity, temperature, and concentration distributions are graphically analyzed and thoroughly discussed. item.title: Three quantum-inspired cores leave opposite fingerprints on the ringing of black holes
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Every black hole hides a question at its center. Einstein's theory predicts that whatever falls in is crushed into a singularity, a point of infinite density where the theory itself breaks down. Most physicists expect quantum gravity to replace that point with something finite. But the center lies hidden behind the horizon. How could we ever learn what is there?
